answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting. Consider a crystal as the anchor of the cost. A vault stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a atlas holds...
